findings.reason: unless the plan states which base a legacy row's payload_ref resolves against (or scopes legacy large-hold replay out explicitly), the node implements one base and silently loses the ability to replay the legacy holds the deliverable promises to preserve.
findings.text: §26's deliverable asserts "every reader of hold records, including the outcomes report and the hold replay, reads the crew-home location and also reads an existing `docs/state` log, so no history is lost", but `replay_hold` resolves a row's `payload_ref` against `replay_hold`'s own `_hold_path(docs, project).parent` (`reckon/crew/picker/outcomes.py:96`) — the same helper §26 repoints at the crew home — so once `_hold_path` moves, a legacy row read from the `docs/state` log has no base to resolve its payload against; 147 rows in `docs/state/reckon/picker-holds.jsonl` alone carry a `payload_ref` with 147 files beside them, and the done-when tests only the new large hold's crew-home payload, leaving the one operation where the two locations differ unmeasured

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_hold_path` (`outcomes.py:193`), `record_picker_hold` (197), `_read_holds` (256), `replay_hold` (82), `_write_hold_payload` (74), `HOLD_PAYLOAD_INLINE_LIMIT` (50) all resolve; `replay.py` holds only `replay`/`_summary` as §26 states; and "one-typesafe-model-picker §32" is the section whose text reads "Store them by reference if they are too large for the row", so the citation resolves.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the declared negative control (the base revision, where the hold lands under `docs/state`) is falsifiable and measurable, but the done-when carries no arm for the one operation the deliverable's "no history is lost" claim depends on, replaying a legacy large hold whose payload_ref points under `docs/state` (see the reasoning finding).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §26 names no gate log, and its cited evidence (the untracked `picker-holds.jsonl` logs and `picker-holds/` payload directories) sits on durable project paths and the crew home, verified on disk: `docs/state/reckon/picker-holds/` is 2.4 MB, matching the plan's "2.4 MB in reckon".
rubric_items.naming: pass — the changed text names functions and files, carries no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag into symbols or comments.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the stated mechanism produces the done-when as written, but not the deliverable's "so no history is lost" claim, because the hold replay's payload base is left unresolved.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §26 carries one deliverable, relocating hold storage to the crew home while every reader keeps reading both locations; the "existing untracked files are left" clause is a constraint, not a second goal.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §26's shared-file hazard with §22 is now serialized by the `plan-section-depends-on` edge `"s22": ["lane-and-model-routing#s26"]`, which matches §26's own text "§22 also writes `outcomes.py` and runs after this section"; §26 itself has no still-open prerequisite (`s20`, which also wrote `outcomes.py`, is `done`).
